title: Byte-wise string handling breaks non-Latin locales
cluster_summary: The root cause is the same in each repo: Lua string functions (%w, #, sub, lower, date %b) work on bytes or the C locale, not on UTF-8 characters, so each addon fails in its own place. No single upstream fix covers all four. The one item that matters is PanelMaster's ASCII-only slug: every fully non-Latin panel name gets the same frame name, so only one such panel can exist. Fix it in PanelMaster together with a UTF-8-aware duplicate guard. KickCD's byte-count truncation should get a file-local UTF-8 prefix helper modelled on MultiMeters' utf8Truncate, not a new LibKa0s surface. AuraMaster's post-translation :lower() and the LibKa0s chart's %b default are latent, so they are optional at most (a comment, and one line in the API doc).

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed in code. Util.Slugify uses gsub('[^%w]+','_'), so Cyrillic, Hangul and Han names all fall back to 'Panel', and frameNameTaken refuses the second one. Accented pairs such as Ärger/Örger collide too. The player sees a clear refusal message, loses no data and can work around it by renaming into ASCII, so medium fits better than high. The smoke rows are LOC-1 to LOC-5; LOC-6 does not exist.
verdicts.remediation: In Util.Slugify, encode the non-%w bytes (for example per-byte hex) so every distinct name gets a distinct slug. Apply it only to newly created or stamped frame names and leave existing records unchanged. In the same change, keep a duplicate-name guard that does not depend on the slug: today the Slugify comment relies on FindByName's ASCII-only lower() plus the slug collision to reject case variants. Without it, 'Übersicht' and 'übersicht' become two panels, against LOC-3. Add headless tests for Cyrillic and CJK uniqueness and for the Ärger/Örger pair. Owner smoke: LOC-1, LOC-2, LOC-3 and LOC-5. Reference PanelMaster#26.

verdicts.assessment: Confirmed. truncateName uses #name and string.sub under a 'Truncate after (characters)' label, and its comment admits it can cut mid-character. The feature is opt-in (default 0) and secret names skip it, but once it is turned on, ruRU and CJK clients get broken glyphs and a cut at roughly 2 to 3 times fewer characters than the label promises. MultiMeters already has a proven pure-Lua utf8Truncate. Two call sites do not justify a new LibKa0s surface with a degraded-stub arm.
verdicts.remediation: Option B: add a file-local UTF-8 prefix helper to KickCD/modules/Castbar.lua that counts lead bytes (mirroring MultiMeters/modules/Row_NameCell.lua utf8Truncate) and rewrite the stale comment at :332-334. Add tests: TruncateName('Éclair de givre', 3) == 'Écl…', valid UTF-8 output, and a CJK case. Promote it to a LibKa0s helper only if this cycle is already cutting a LibKa0s release for other reasons.

verdicts.assessment: The code does apply :lower() after translation at OptionsSetup.lua:419-420, but only enUS.lua ships, so there is no effect today. Dropping :lower() would change the visible enUS picker casing and the matching tests for a speculative benefit.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: add a one-line comment that the :lower() assumes enUS-only labels. When a non-enUS locale is added, switch to whole-phrase translation keys instead of a post-translation case transform.

verdicts.assessment: WidgetsLineChart.lua:304 defaults to date('%d %b', x), and LootHistory's Timeline passes no formatX. Whether WoW's date() returns C-locale English on deDE or frFR clients has not been checked in-client, and the real fix belongs to a consumer that is out of scope here.
verdicts.remediation: Optional: add one sentence to the WidgetsLineChart API doc saying the default formatX uses date('%d %b') (C-locale month abbreviation), so localized hosts should pass formatX. Track the LootHistory formatX change as an issue, and only after the owner confirms the English %b output in-client.
